html:
The Cañari are an Andean people of southern Ecuador, in today's provinces of Cañar and Azuay. Before the Inca they formed an independent confederation of chiefdoms, with a centre at Guapondélig, near modern Cuenca.

They resisted the Inca fiercely, but Topa Inca conquered them in the later 1400s. The Inca built Tomebamba on the site of Guapondélig as a second capital, and Huayna Capac was born there by most accounts. They also built Ingapirca beside a Cañari shrine. Many Cañari were moved away as colonists to other parts of the empire. In the Inca civil war they sided with Huáscar, and Atahualpa punished them harshly. So when the Spanish came, the Cañari joined them and fought beside Pizarro's men. Their descendants still live around Cañar and speak Kichwa.
